How did SCRIPE remediate Emailing, Multi-DB Persistence, and Admin Onboarding across Backend and Frontend?

Long image

A

Answer

SCRIPE eliminated silent email drops, CommunicationDbContext persistence loss, and 13 OWASP vulnerabilities across 94 backend and 22 frontend files. Every onboarding invitation, manual email, and template write now executes in active DI scope, flushes to the right schema, and passes 3,617 unit tests plus 4/4 live Playwright E2E tests.1

  1. CreateAdminCommandHandler, RegisterTenantSelfServiceCommandHandler, and SignupCheckoutCompletedEventHandler resolve tenant URLs in active request scope and enqueue durable jobs through IEmailQueue instead of detached Task.Run closures.1
  2. All 4 email commands and 5 message-template commands in Core.Application now call SaveChangesAsync on CommunicationDbContext repositories instead of the IdentityDbContext-bound global IUnitOfWork.2
  3. EmailSecurityPolicies and EmailAttachmentPathPolicy block container path traversal, one-time token replay, Scriban template injection, unencoded HTML fields, and raw PII logging.3
  4. Next.js 16 AdminsView, SetupAccountView, and Communication modules display Pending Setup badges, preserve setup tokens across URL scrubbing, deduplicate CC/BCC sends, and match MessageTemplate validator limits.4

Applies toSCRIPE MonorepoSlices 6F, 6G & 7A-fix

How does the remediated emailing and onboarding architecture connect end to end?

Diagram structure
  • Admin & Setup SPA fe_admin
  • Composer & Template SPA fe_comm
  • Identity Onboarding CQRS id_handlers
  • Email & Template CQRS comm_handlers
  • IdentityDbContext Schema id_db
  • Policy & Scriban Shield sec_shield
  • Priority IEmailQueue email_queue
  • EmailJobProcessor & Retry job_proc
  • CommunicationDbContext comm_db
  • Resend, SMTP & Dev Senders transport
  • fe_admin → id_handlers · Create & Activate
  • fe_comm → comm_handlers · Encrypted IDs
  • id_handlers → id_db · Save Token
  • id_handlers → email_queue · In-Scope Queue
  • comm_handlers → sec_shield · Validate
  • sec_shield → comm_db · Repo Save
  • email_queue → job_proc · Queue("emails")
  • job_proc → comm_db · Per-Row Save
  • job_proc → transport · TLS Dispatch

Frontend admin and communication views call encrypted-ID REST endpoints. Handlers resolve tenant metadata in active request scope, persist to IdentityDbContext or CommunicationDbContext, and enqueue priority background workers.

  1. Admin & Setup SPA ↗

    AdminsView displays Pending Setup badges and mode-aware toasts while SetupAccountView retains the setup token after stripping ?token= from the URL bar.

  2. Identity Onboarding CQRS ↗

    CreateAdmin, RegisterTenantSelfService, and SignupCheckoutCompleted resolve tenant URLs in active scope and enqueue jobs via IEmailQueue.

  3. Email & Template CQRS ↗

    All 4 email commands and 5 template commands flush CommunicationDbContext directly and encrypt every returned ID via IIdEncryptionService.

  4. Policy & Scriban Shield ↗

    Enforces EmailAttachmentPathPolicy, SafeContainerNameRegex, bounded Scriban TemplateContext, H(...) encoding, and SafeHttpUrl.

  5. EmailJobProcessor & Retry ↗

    Processes ["critical", "emails", "default"] queues, flushes CommunicationDbContext per email, and excludes one-time auth tokens from retries.

  6. Resend, SMTP & Dev Senders ↗

    Disposes MailMessage and streams, enforces non-Development SSL and provider checks, quotes RFC-5322 names, and masks logged email PII.

Why did CreateAdmin setup emails fail while Resend worked, and how was onboarding fixed?

Diagram structure
  • Admin & Setup UI ui
  • CreateAdminHandler create_h
  • AccountSetupService setup_svc
  • IdentityDbContext id_db
  • IEmailQueue Worker queue
  • ui → create_h · POST /api/v1/admins (sendSetupEmail=true)
  • create_h → id_db · Resolve TenantUrl + Persist Admin & TokenHash
  • create_h → queue · QueueEmailAsync(AccountSetup) -> [Queue("emails")]
  • create_h → ui · 201 EncryptedId + Invitation Toast
  • ui → setup_svc · POST /api/v1/account-setup/resend
  • setup_svc → id_db · Snapshot Old Token -> Save Fresh TokenHash
  • setup_svc → ui · Restore Snapshot & Skip Cooldown if Send Fails
  • ui → setup_svc · POST /api/v1/account-setup/activate (X-Setup-Token)
  • setup_svc → id_db · Tx: TryConsumeToken -> MutatePwd -> CustomFields
  • setup_svc → ui · 200 Activated (Pending Setup -> Active)

Previously, CreateAdminCommandHandler wrapped URL resolution and email sending inside an unawaited _ = Task.Run(...) closure after returning the HTTP response. When ASP.NET Core disposed the request scope, ITenantUrlResolver queried a disposed IdentityDbContext, threw ObjectDisposedException, and swallowed the failure into a warning log.1

  1. CreateAdminHandler ↗

    Validates required email when SendSetupEmail is true, resolves GetTenantUrlAsync before scope disposal, and enqueues AccountSetup via IEmailQueue.

  2. IEmailQueue Worker ↗

    Routes AccountSetup to the "emails" Hangfire queue (ranked ahead of "default") or bounded 3-attempt EmailQueueWorker in Native mode.

  3. AccountSetupService ↗

    Restores the previous token snapshot without arming the 60s cooldown or 3/hr cap if dispatch fails, and persists custom fields only after atomic token consumption.

  4. Admin & Setup UI ↗

    Shows Pending Setup in AdminsView without any manual resend click and keeps the captured token in SetupAccountView after history.replaceState.

How was the CommunicationDbContext vs IdentityDbContext UnitOfWork split-brain resolved?

In SCRIPE's modular monolith, Identity.Infrastructure registers the global IUnitOfWork against IdentityDbContext, while SentEmailLogRepository and MessageTemplateRepository run on CommunicationDbContext (communication schema). Every email and template command in Core.Application previously mutated CommunicationDbContext entities and called _unitOfWork.SaveChangesAsync(), flushing IdentityDbContext and silently discarding all communication writes.2

Diagram structure
  • Email or Template Command cmd_in
  • Attachment & Ownership OK? att_gate
  • IgnoreQueryFilters Lookup tmpl_load
  • Bounded Scriban & Sanitizer scriban_box
  • Repo SaveChangesAsync comm_save
  • Return Encrypted ID enc_out
  • Non-Auth Transient Retry? retry_gate
  • att_gate → tmpl_load · yes
  • cmd_in → att_gate · Validate
  • comm_save → enc_out · Encrypt(Guid)
  • comm_save → retry_gate · Background Poll
  • scriban_box → comm_save · Evict Cache
  • tmpl_load → scriban_box · Tenant or Global
  1. Email or Template Command ↗

    Validates 50,000-char bodies, 2,000-char DesignVariables, single-address CC/BCC limits (<= 50), and caller tenant ownership.

  2. Attachment & Ownership OK? ↗

    EmailAttachmentPathPolicy restricts paths to email-attachments/<file> (<= 10 files, <= 10 MB) and verifies tenant access via CanAccessFileQuery.

  3. IgnoreQueryFilters Lookup ↗

    MessageTemplateRepository uses .IgnoreQueryFilters() so tenants resolve their own override first and fall back to global (TenantId == null) seeded templates.

  4. Bounded Scriban & Sanitizer ↗

    TemplateRenderer caps LoopLimit = 100 and LimitToString = 100,000, HTML-encodes scalar placeholders, sanitizes custom HTML, and evicts cache on writes.

  5. Repo SaveChangesAsync ↗

    Calls _logRepo.SaveChangesAsync or _templateRepo.SaveChangesAsync directly on CommunicationDbContext and returns _idEncryption.Encrypt(id).

  6. Non-Auth Transient Retry? ↗

    EmailJobProcessor saves per row, while MessageRetryJob and ResendEmailCommand block OneTimeTokenTemplateKeys and EmailSenderRole.Auth.

Diagram structure
  • identity.admins identity_admins
  • communication.message_templates comm_templates
  • communication.sent_email_logs comm_email_logs
  • comm_email_logs → comm_templates · renders key
  • comm_email_logs → identity_admins · recipient_id

How are all 13 OWASP security findings and template contracts enforced?

All 4 P0 Critical, 6 P1 High, and 3 P2 Medium vulnerabilities identified in #395 and #397 are closed in production code and locked by dedicated regression suites.3

Strict Separation Between Seeded Theme Templates and Custom HTML

Platform-seeded templates (TenantId == null) carry RenderedMessage.IsPlatformTemplate = true so ScripeEmailTheme <style> blocks (dark-mode sx-* classes and @media queries) stay intact while scalar placeholders are HTML-encoded before Scriban evaluation. Tenant-authored templates and /api/v1/message-templates/preview always pass through MessageTemplateBodySanitizer and HtmlAllowlistSanitizer.SanitizeEmail.
